source_identity.title: Multilayer jamming-reinforced inflatable systems for rapidly deployable lightweight construction
source_identity.local_path: data/inbox/2026-Multilayer jamming-reinforced inflatable systems for rapidly deployable lightweight construction.pdf

identity_verification.pdf_page_1: title, complete author list, journal volume/article number and DOI printed on PDF p. 1
identity_verification.pdfinfo: 17 pages; matching title, journal/DOI subject and first author

fulltext_state.scope: single named source; no broad search or final K adjudication

page_grounded_evidence.statement: The stated contributions are system integration, layer-stiffness selection, pressure/layer/loading experiments, cyclic energy dissipation, and preliminary analysis/design guidance.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Defines the paper’s research objective; no validity-map contribution is claimed.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: Vacuum-induced interlayer friction changes coupling in an MLJ stack; the system couples an upper MLJ plate, inflatable airbeam, and optional aramid ropes.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Direct physical-system and mechanism overlap.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: The n-layer beam formulas give pre-slip deflection, interface shear, slip onset and load limits for simply supported and fixed-support cases. The authors expressly limit these expressions to the initial vacuum-on pre-slip stage and parameter estimation, not post-slip large-deformation prediction.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Reduced analytical M exists, but its stated prediction scope is limited.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: The authors cite prior sequential-slip and DIC work and state that detailed nonlinear sliding evolution is not further elaborated for their application.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Post-slip interface evolution is not the studied model-validity object.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: The six material–structure regimes depend on slip-initiation, allowable, and material deformation. The figure is described as qualitative material-selection guidance with approximate rather than strict quantitative boundaries.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: The regime map concerns physical/material suitability.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: The load-enhancement expression approximates post-slip load by pre-slip load plus a full-slip contribution, neglecting the difficult-to-predict partial-slip contribution. A 20% minimum enhancement is given as an example design-benefit threshold.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Physical performance threshold must not be mistaken for model-error tolerance.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: Separate plates contain 10 or 20 SC-AF layers, each 600 × 200 mm with 1 mm TPU outer film. Dead weights and laser midspan deflection are used at vacuum settings 0, −20, −40, −60, −80, −100 kPa. Hinged/sliding and restrained-angle supports are tested.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: E role: component tests span layer number, vacuum, support and load.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: Some intermediate points were skipped, deflections could exceed sensor range, vacuum control fluctuated within ±0.002 MPa, and sensor/control limits affected the pressure sweep.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Experimental resolution limits matter for any boundary claim.

page_grounded_evidence.locator: p. 7 Fig. 6 and Eq. (20); p. 8 Table 2
page_grounded_evidence.statement: The authors back-calculate an effective friction coefficient from stepped loading and say the exact instability-onset load cannot be identified accurately; the coefficient is an effective parameter, not a unique material constant.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Model parameters are extracted from experiment, limiting independence for model-form error isolation.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: Hinged 20-layer plates show sudden kink/hinge-like deformation attributed to imperfections and slip redistribution; fixed-angle plates show smoother response, and pressure regulation produces history effects.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Physical slip/instability regimes and fixture effects are observed.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: The integrated prototype is 1 m long, 200 mm wide, about 100 mm inflated height, with SC-AF layers of about 0.26 mm each and semi-cylindrical supports.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Geometry and boundary context for model–experiment comparison.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: A 300 × 90 × 8 mm loading plate and four reference/vacuum/cable/combined configurations are used. Airbeam pressures are 5, 10, 20 kPa with ±1 kPa accuracy. Table 3 reports 3 mm chord stiffness and peak load.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: E role and output definitions for structural response, distinct from D1 model-form errors.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: Quasi-static cycles at 5, 10, 20 kPa use imposed amplitudes 10–120 mm; the 10 mm case is excluded from loop-area analysis because of signal noise. Dissipated energy is the hysteresis-loop area; only lowest-point displacement is measured and energy values are described as conservative.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: E role: cyclic physical response, not independent boundary-crossing model validation.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: The authors adapt a circular inflated-beam formulation to a rectangular airbeam through an equivalent radius and pressure-dependent reduction factor Cp; Eq. (25) is an approximate upper-bound scaling relation and Eq. (26) a deflection-trend approximation.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Additional simplified M; stated assumptions limit precision.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: Three response regimes are defined by relative MLJ sliding/yield and airbeam buckling loads: MLJ yields first, near-simultaneous mechanisms, or airbeam buckles first. The 10 kPa condition is interpreted as the most balanced coupling.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Physical failure-sequence boundary, not an accepted/rejected model-validity boundary.

page_grounded_evidence.locator: p. 15 Discussion bullet “Model–experiment comparison and interpretation”; Eqs. (8),(25)
page_grounded_evidence.statement: The simplified predictions are about 27, 55, 110 N for airbeam buckling at 5, 10, 20 kPa and about 28 N for planar MLJ yield. Authors state these are significantly below experiments and that the simplified model misses load-transfer mechanisms.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Direct observed model–experiment discrepancy, with numerical examples but no defined error metric.

page_grounded_evidence.locator: p. 15 same bullet; Fig. 9 on p. 10
page_grounded_evidence.statement: The paper attributes discrepancy partly to finite distributed loading (estimated 18% effect) and chiefly to shallow curvature, semi-cylindrical-support restraint and contact confinement that create shell-like force paths.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Mechanistic hypothesis for discrepancy; strongest overlap with D1 why-model-fails question.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: A representative geometry-dependent factor range α≈0.2–0.5 is adopted, yielding an effective MLJ yield-load estimate of about 56–140 N; authors call the formulation conceptual rather than precise predictive and say advanced shell/cross-section/post-buckling models are needed.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Explicit model limitation; factor is not an independently validated interface-resolved reference.

page_grounded_evidence.locator: p. 15 Discussion bullet “Experimental setup and stiffness measurement”
page_grounded_evidence.statement: The authors note pneumatic-control limits, a single repeatedly loaded prototype with gradual stiffness degradation, and complex low-pressure hysteresis.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Uncertainty and repeatability limitations.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: TPU outer-membrane modifications to pre-slip deflection, interface shear and sliding limits are derived.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Clarifies analytical model scope; not a full-layer contact reference.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: No independent higher-fidelity, interface-resolved numerical reference or M-versus-R quantitative comparison is reported in the inspected full text.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Missing R role for D1-equivalent workflow.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: No output-specific model-form error metric, predeclared model-error acceptance tolerance, or deliberately sampled both-side model-validity boundary is reported. The p. 5 20% example is a design-benefit threshold.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Separates physical and model validity criteria.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: The precise numeric layer count used in each integrated airbeam test is not explicit in the inspected description; do not transfer the 10/20-layer plate-test counts to the integrated prototype.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Prevents invented operating-domain metadata.

page_grounded_evidence.statement: The original T2 disposition is metadata/abstract-only, unresolved and blocking at the time of W10.
page_grounded_evidence.D1_threat_role: Preserves the historical state-at-time.

INTERPRETATION.statement: The paper maps material/structural response regimes; it does not map a declared model-validity domain.

LIMITATION.statement: The physical response map may still motivate D1 operating-domain design.
This is a bounded finding about this 17-page PDF, not an assertion about unpublished work.

INTERPRETATION.statement: Numerical prediction/measurement differences are discussed, but no defined output-specific model-form error over a domain is quantified.

LIMITATION.statement: The reported load numbers permit external calculations but such calculations would be our derivation, not an author metric.

INTERPRETATION.statement: No predeclared model-error acceptance/breakdown criterion is reported.

LIMITATION.statement: The example 20% design enhancement and physical load-crossing regimes are different criteria.

INTERPRETATION.statement: Experiments vary pressure, layers, supports and cyclic amplitude, but do not deliberately sample both sides of a predicted model-validity boundary.

LIMITATION.statement: Physical mechanism transitions are observed and can inform future boundary sampling.

INTERPRETATION.statement: The paper proposes plausible discrepancy mechanisms—curvature, distributed loading, contact confinement and shell-like load paths—but does not isolate them with an interface-resolved reference or local causality tests.

LIMITATION.statement: Author causal explanation is distinguished from independently demonstrated cause.

INTERPRETATION.statement: The paper contains simplified M and physical E roles, without D1-equivalent R or validity/error-map logic; a complete equivalent M→R→E workflow is not demonstrated.

LIMITATION.statement: M and E are substantive overlaps.

INTERPRETATION.statement: It makes analytical modeling, parameter sweeps, and model–experiment discussion established practice in MLJ systems; it alone does not show D1’s surviving narrow scientific act is merely routine.

LIMITATION.statement: No final novelty judgment is made; W12 must evaluate the full corpus.

INTERPRETATION.statement: Conceptual overlap is material in system, slip mechanism, reduced model, experiment and failure discussion; the paper does not answer the same validity-boundary question with interface-resolved R and predeclared error criteria.

LIMITATION.statement: Different airbeam geometry alone is not the basis for distinction.

what_it_proves.statement: The paper derives simplified pre-slip and inflatable-beam estimates, measures MLJ plate and integrated airbeam response over declared conditions, and explicitly discusses mismatches and likely structural causes.

what_it_does_not_prove.statement: Within the inspected full text, it does not establish an interface-resolved R comparison, output-specific model-form error map, predeclared acceptance criterion or independent experiment across a predicted model-validity boundary.

K1.rationale: Reduced model and regime language; distinguish physical regimes from model validity.

K2.rationale: M exists; no interface-resolved R comparison.

K3.rationale: Numerical discrepancy is reported; model-form error is not isolated.

K4.rationale: Physical boundaries and example benefit threshold need timing/role separation.

K5.rationale: Substantial experiments, without both-side model-validity sampling.

K6.rationale: Discussion supplies mechanistic hypotheses for discrepancy.

K7.rationale: M and E overlap; R and validity workflow absent in inspected PDF.

K8.rationale: Analytical/experimental steps are precedented; full scientific act unresolved to W12.

K9.rationale: Conceptual equivalence must weigh substantial system/mechanism overlap and missing R/validity elements.

successor_disposition_basis.statement: Material physical, model, experiment and discrepancy overlap; the full text does not document the complete narrowed D1 M→R→E validity/breakdown act. This is a W10 source disposition only.

audit_method.method: SHA-256 and pdfinfo identity checks; pdftotext -layout inspection of PDF pages 1–17; manual locator mapping to printed page numbers and section/equation/figure/table labels

unresolved_evidence_gaps.statement: Exact layer count of integrated airbeam MLJ component is not explicit in §3.2.1.
Underlying raw measurements and uncertainty needed for independent output-specific discrepancy estimates are not supplied by this audit.
